pairs.subject: feed
pairs.evidence: app/(studio)/projects/runs/_runs/Runs.tsx:3 Runs is a horizontal day-line: jobs are bars placed by start and end on resource-lane rows, with zoom and a centred NOW, not a newest-first list of occurrences read top-down. A case-insensitive grep of app/(studio)/projects/runs for unseen, lastSeen, markRead, prepend, readPosition, 'new since', 'newest first' and cluster found nothing, so the feed contract (catch-up order, prepend, read anchor, clustering, retention) has no surface here to govern.

techniques.evidence: app/(studio)/projects/runs/_runs/view.ts:124 The only ordering is the J/K walk, ascending by start with a key tiebreak, so it is total and three-way. Placement is otherwise by x-position on a time axis; there is no newest-first sequence.

app/(studio)/projects/runs/_runs/Runs.tsx:101 The 'live feed' is SSE advice that triggers a coalesced router.refresh() of the whole model. No rows grow at a top edge, so there is no viewport to hold and no held-arrivals buffer.
app/(studio)/projects/runs/_runs/view.ts:32 Rows are fixed resource lanes, not occurrence rows. A busy producer fills its own lane and cannot drown others.
app/(studio)/projects/runs/_runs/Runs.tsx:51 The only reader state is selection and zoom in the URL. There is no 'since you last looked' promise and no badge.

app/(studio)/projects/runs/_runs/model.ts:38 The window is a fixed span around NOW, read from the ledger, which this context does not own or reap. A hit on the LEDGER_CAP cap is stated as truncation (load.ts:487), not drawn as empty.

pairs.registryProposal: The feed golden path draws boundaries against table, triage queue, transcript and audit record, but not against a time-axis/Gantt surface (bars placed on resource rows by start and end). A day-line that follows live work through a module named 'liveFeed' scores high lexically against 'feed' but has none of its contract. Naming the timeline as a neighbour would spare judges this false match.
